blocks.prompt: 4 If \(\omega\) is a root of \(x^{2}+x+1=0\), show that its other root is \(\omega^{2}\) and hence prove that \(\omega^{3}=1\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh quadratic equation ke roots wala sawal hai. Humein bataya gaya hai ke \(\omega\) equation \(x^{2}+x+1=0\) ka ek root hai; humein doosra root find karna hai aur phir \(\omega^{3}=1\) saabit karna hai. Yahan woh do formulas kaam aate hain jo aap roots ke baare mein parh chuke hain: \(ax^{2}+bx+c=0\) ke roots ka sum (jama) \(-\frac{b}{a}\) aur product (zarb) \(\frac{c}{a}\) hota hai. Plan: pehle likhein ke "\(\omega\) root hai" ka matlab kya hai, phir sum of roots se doosra root nikaalein, aur aakhir mein product of roots se \(\omega^{3}=1\) saabit karein.
steps:
Step 1: "Omega root hai" ka matlab
\[\omega^{2}+\omega+1=0\]
\[\omega^{2}=-1-\omega\]
Kyun: Root woh value hai jo \(x\) ki jagah rakhne se equation sach ho jaaye. Is liye \(x\) ki jagah \(\omega\) rakha. Phir \(\omega^{2}\) ko akela kiya; yeh shakal agle step mein kaam aayegi.

Step 2: Sum of roots se doosra root
\[\omega+\beta=-\dfrac{b}{a}=-1\]
\[\beta=-1-\omega\]
\[\beta=\omega^{2}\]
Kyun: Is equation mein \(a=b=c=1\) hain. Doosre root ko \(\beta\) (beta) kaha. Sum of roots se \(\beta=-1-\omega\) mila, aur Step 1 batata hai ke \(-1-\omega\) bilkul \(\omega^{2}\) hai. Is liye doosra root \(\omega^{2}\) hai.

Step 3: Product of roots se omega cubed = 1
\[\omega\cdot\beta=\dfrac{c}{a}=1\]
\[\omega\cdot\omega^{2}=1\]
\[\omega^{3}=1\]
Kyun: Ab dono roots maloom hain, \(\omega\) aur \(\omega^{2}\). Un ka product \(\frac{c}{a}=1\) hona chahiye. Same base ki powers multiply karne par indices jama hote hain: \(\omega^{1+2}=\omega^{3}\).
Dhyan dein: product of roots \(\frac{c}{a}\) hai, \(-\frac{c}{a}\) nahin; minus sirf sum wale formula mein hai.

Tasdeeq: omega squared bhi equation ko satisfy karta hai
\[(\omega^{2})^{2}+\omega^{2}+1=\omega^{4}+\omega^{2}+1\]
\[=\omega+\omega^{2}+1=0\]
Kyun: \(\omega^{3}=1\) se \(\omega^{4}=\omega\). Rakhne par expression zero aaya, yaani \(\omega^{2}\) waqai root hai. (Ek aur raasta: \(x^{3}-1=(x-1)(x^{2}+x+1)\), to jo bhi \(x^{2}+x+1\) ko zero kare woh \(x^{3}-1\) ko bhi zero karega, yaani \(\omega^{3}-1=0\).)
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: doosra root \(\omega^{2}\) hai, aur \(\omega^{3}=1\). Matlab: \(x^{2}+x+1=0\) ke dono roots hi 1 ke complex cube roots hain.
